subject: System Design
title: WebSockets and Real-Time
description: Learn WebSockets and Real-Time in one minute.

hook.text: In a chat app, messages appear instantly without refreshing. That's WebSockets, not regular HTTP.

buildup.text: HTTP is request-response: the client asks, the server answers. WebSockets keep a persistent connection open.

discovery.text: Once connected, either side can send data at any time. This enables real-time chat, gaming, and dashboards.

twist.text: WebSocket connections consume server memory. At millions of connections, the cost adds up fast.

climax.text: WebSockets trade efficiency for immediacy — essential for real-time, overkill for everything else.

punchline.text: A connection that stays open for instant data.

quiz.question: How do WebSockets differ from HTTP?
options: They keep a persistent two-way connection open
